record.paper_title: Formal languages and arithmetic theories: recent results and open problems
record.context_brief: Relative existential definability of regular predicates
record.original_question: Fix a base p and alphabet Sigma = {0, ..., p - 1}. For a regular language L over Sigma*, let [L] be the set of natural numbers represented by the p-ary encodings in L, treated as a unary predicate on N. Given two regular languages L1 and L2, is it decidable whether the predicate [L1] is definable by an existential first-order formula over the structure (N, 0, 1, +, [L2], <=), where the only language-specific predicate available to the formula is membership in [L2]?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Fix an integer base $p \geq 2$ and let $\Sigma = \{0, 1, \dots, p-1\}$. For a finite word $w = a_k a_{k-1} \cdots a_0 \in \Sigma^*$, let $\mathrm{val}_p(w) = \sum_{i=0}^{k} a_i p^i \in \mathbb{N}$. For a regular language $L \subseteq \Sigma^*$, define the unary predicate $[L] := \{\mathrm{val}_p(w) : w \in L\} \subseteq \mathbb{N}$.

Consider the first-order structure $\mathcal{M}_{L_2} = \langle \mathbb{N}, 0, 1, +, \leq, [L_2] \rangle$, where $[L_2]$ is interpreted as a unary predicate symbol and no other language-specific predicate is available. A subset $S \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ is said to be existentially definable in $\mathcal{M}_{L_2}$ if there is a first-order formula $\varphi(x)$ in the signature of $\mathcal{M}_{L_2}$ whose quantifier prefix consists only of existential quantifiers, such that $S = \{n \in \mathbb{N} : \mathcal{M}_{L_2} \models \varphi(n)\}$.

Problem. Is there an algorithm that, given as input two regular languages $L_1, L_2 \subseteq \Sigma^*$ (presented by finite automata or regular expressions), decides whether $[L_1]$ is existentially definable in $\mathcal{M}_{L_2}$?
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem in surveys on formal languages and arithmetic theories. Related work (e.g., on existential arithmetic with addition and bitwise minimum) characterizes existentially definable relations as automaton-recognizable in certain structures but does not resolve the parameterized decidability question for arbitrary regular $L_1, L_2$. No source found announcing a decidability resolution.

status_evidence.title: On the Existential Arithmetics with Addition and Bitwise Minimum
status_evidence.snippet: Existentially definable relations in (N,+,bitwise-min) coincide with a class of automaton-recognizable relations.
status_evidence.claim: Relates existential definability over expansions of (N,+) to automata, but does not settle the decidability of the relative existential-definability problem for arbitrary regular predicates.
